newsitem.title: UK: UK's Camelot reviewing options in pay row.
newsitem.headline: UK's Camelot reviewing options in pay row.

text.p: UK national lottery operator Camelot Group Plc said reports three executives could quit in a row over bonuses were "speculative".

The Financial Times reported on Thursday that Camelot chief executive Tim Holley, finance director Peter Murphy and communications director David Rigg may resign in the next 24 hours over a row that his pitted them against National Heritage Secretary Chris Smith.
Smith, the cabinet minister responsible for the arts and culture, wants the executives to hand over some of their controversial bonuses to charity. He has demanded a reponse by the end of the week.
Camelot's five shareholders are expected to meet on Thursday afternoon or Friday morning to discuss how to defuse the row.
"A range of options is being considered," a Camelot spokeswoman said, refusing to go into details.
Camelot has been at the centre of a political storm after the bonuses inflated its annual executive salary bill 40 percent to 2.35 million stg last year, while sums raised for good causes fell.
Camelot is a consortium of Racal Electronics Plc, De La Rue Plc, GTECH, Cadbury Schweppes Plc and Fujitsu Ltd's ICL.
Camelot chairman Sir George Russell told Smith this week that the consortium would examine ways of turning the lottery into a not-for-profit operation.
But some of the consortium's shareholders are reported to oppose the plan.
